clue.text: Catholic city half-backing Scottish club

indicators.note: only the front half of the club's name is turned to run backwards, the rest stays in order

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
Celtic is the Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A Catholic city is partly supporting a Scottish football club, Celtic having Catholic roots.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholic with a capital C looks religious, especially beside Celtic; here it is the lower-case sense of wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means broad and wide-ranging in taste, the same as drawing from many sources.

clue.text: Purge of Sophoclean sensibilities

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters come from inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is cutting the Greek playwright Sophocles' tragic sensibilities out of a production.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge something is to clean it out thoroughly, ridding it of impurities, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Spare chap with a very small part?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: additional, more than needed

definitions.text: chap with a very small part?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a film actor in a crowd scene with no lines

explanation.surface: A spare man with a very small part sounds like a body-shaming joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: the tiny part is a role on screen, not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare item is one over and above, and a walk-on film actor in the background is also called this.

clue.text: Papers showing stock pickets tear up

indicators.note: torn up means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Striking pickets rip up the papers that show stock prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticker tape is the paper strip that printed stock prices from a telegraph ticker.
explanation.definitionFit: These paper strips once carried live share prices from the exchange, so they are papers recording stock movements.

clue.text: Prison housing belonging to US brewery once

indicators.note: something housing another thing holds it within its walls

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

explanation.surface: A prison in America housing an old brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: US looks like America; it is the plain pronoun us. Courage was a long-established London brewery, now a brand only.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage was a famous British brewing company whose own brewery has since closed, hence a brewery of the past.

clue.text: Not completely wild about party hat

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps another
not completely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone is half-keen on a party hat.
explanation.walkthrough: FERA is the wild word cut short; it then wraps the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, an example of the category.

clue.text: Short argument about relationship

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run back to front
short means the word is cut and loses its final letter

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A brief row about a relationship between a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit describes how well two things match or correspond, as in a good fit between partners.

clue.text: Church supporting tax cut from Maastricht?

indicators.note: a cut word has its end trimmed off
in a down clue, supporting means sitting below, so it comes after

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church backing a tax cut decided in Maastricht, home of the EU treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: Maastricht evokes the EU treaty and tax policy, but it is simply a city in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Maastricht is a Netherlands city, so a person or thing from there is of that nationality, by example.

clue.text: Bitter US agency beginning to lambaste Schwarzenegger film

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A sour American agency starts to lay into an Arnold Schwarzenegger movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw Deal is a 1986 action movie starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, so the title names that picture.

clue.text: Split now, with dog having done one

indicators.note: to do one is slang for leaving, so this part has gone from the word

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A couple split up now that the dog has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do one' is British slang for clear off; the dog leaves the word for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as a noun is a tear or split, and as a past participle means torn apart.

clue.text: York? Noble, yet heartless, individual

indicators.note: with no heart, the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: one's own is individual to oneself

explanation.surface: York, an aristocrat stripped of courage, standing alone.
explanation.walkthrough: York is the old administrative centre of Yorkshire; the question mark signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A county town is the administrative seat of an English county, and York traditionally held that role for Yorkshire.

clue.text: Popular head of media had one canned!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A popular media boss has had someone fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Canned looks like sacked; it is slang for imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the can is slang for being in prison, so someone canned is a prisoner.

clue.text: Got off with a journalist around fire

indicators.note: around means the first words surround what follows

parts.note: to light is to set on fire

explanation.surface: Someone got off with a reporter beside the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Got off looks like romance; it means stepped down from a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step down from a bus or train, so the past tense means disembarked.

clue.text: Gin friend upset collaring old pointer?

indicators.note: collaring means grabbing round the neck, so one piece encloses another
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinking pal is upset at grabbing an old dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointer looks like the gun dog; the question mark signals the digit used for pointing.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger is the digit people extend to indicate things, so it is a pointer by function.

clue.text: US conscript chosen to appear in court

indicators.note: to appear in means to be placed inside another word

parts.note: to see someone is to court or date them
elect means chosen, as in the president-elect

explanation.surface: An American draftee chosen to appear before a court.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks legal; it means romancing, as in seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US, a person picked by the draft board for military service was called by this term.

clue.text: Tree seasonal worker trimmed close to gym

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: an elf works for Father Christmas

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A seasonal worker trims a tree near the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasonal worker suggests a fruit picker; it is a Christmas elf.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a deciduous broadleaf, a familiar example of the category of tall woodland plants.

clue.text: Stuffed shirt ignoring tenor's two fingers?

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a doublet was a padded, stuffed jacket
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A pompous man ignores a tenor's rude two-fingered gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffed shirt looks like a pompous person; it is the padded Tudor garment. Spirit measures are judged by fingers in the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A twice-sized spirit measure fills the glass about two finger-widths deep, hence the question mark.

clue.text: College: an association of people avoiding working

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so a part is removed

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A college described as a body of people who shirk work.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is students avoiding work; the trade union drops its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal British short form for university, an institution of higher learning.

clue.text: Welsh member in an excited state for foreplay?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for Welsh
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Welshman with an excited member, a saucy picture of foreplay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is bawdy, but the question mark points to the exercise done before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Light exercise before sport is preparation before play, so the question mark allows this cheeky reading.

clue.text: When to tackle cold duke about my grants

indicators.note: to tackle someone is to wrap arms round them, so one piece goes around another
about means surrounding, so the pair of letters goes either side

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
C for cold on a tap
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Questions of when to confront a chilly duke over the speaker's grants.
explanation.walkthrough: My is the exclamation, not the possessive; cor is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord means to give or bestow, so it is a verb synonym for grants.

clue.text: Diamond heist at sea, nine tons to split!

indicators.note: to split something is to go into the middle of it
at sea means confused and adrift, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A diamond robbery on the water, nine tons of loot to divide up.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamond looks like a gem in a heist; it is the anniversary or jubilee name.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond anniversary or jubilee marks sixty years, so diamond stands for that ordinal.

clue.text: Rather blue commercial with Southern beauty hosting it

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, and it points back at the earlier word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a dish is an attractive person

explanation.surface: A rather risque advert featuring a Southern belle.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue suggests risque, matching the beauty; here it means a little down.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means low in spirits, and the suffix softens it to somewhat unhappy.

clue.text: Flag setter placed around Republican ship

indicators.note: placed around means wrapped about another letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A flag set around a Republican ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a banner; it is the verb meaning weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars, an example of a warship.

clue.text: Damned used car explodes outside club

indicators.note: outside means surrounding another letter
something that explodes is blown into pieces, which land in a new order

explanation.surface: A cursed second-hand car blows up outside a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Damned and this word both mean under a curse or doomed, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Family member is dirty, having pinched bottom twice!

indicators.note: pinching the bottom twice takes off the last letter two times

explanation.surface: A lecherous relative caught pinching someone's bottom twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a seedy relative; bottom means the last letter of the down word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a relative, an example of a member of one's family.

clue.text: One's mate missing out on North Island

parts.note: I is one, so one's is I'S

indicators.note: missing out on means not getting, so a letter is lost

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate for mate

explanation.surface: Someone's friend misses a trip to a northern island.
explanation.walkthrough: China for mate is Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is a volcanic Italian island in the Bay of Naples, a named example.

clue.text: Diary found in empty campus blocks

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the other word
an empty word has had its middle removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a log is a record or diary

explanation.surface: A diary found in the empty blocks of a deserted campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks looks like buildings; here it is a verb, obstructs.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog something is to obstruct it, so a verb that also means jams up.

clue.text: Type of riding stick on royal in windy city

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in an across clue
in means placed inside the other word
windy means twisting, so the letters wind into a new order

parts.note: R for royal, as in RN
to stick to is to cling

explanation.surface: A riding style with a royal sticking on in a windy city such as Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: Windy city hints at Chicago; windy is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a three-wheeled cycle is one form of riding, so this activity names a kind of it.

clue.text: Better complain if queen's blown off

indicators.note: blown off means removed, so a letter disappears

explanation.surface: It is better to grumble if the queen has blown someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is a verb here, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap a story is to top or outdo it, so a verb synonym of better.

clue.text: Archdeacon after the heart of Tom Baker?

indicators.note: after means coming later in the order
the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the Venerable is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: An archdeacon is chasing the actor Tom Baker, the fourth Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Baker looks like the actor; Baker alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is something that bakes, and the kitchen appliance that cooks bread does exactly that.

clue.text: Dead large stash of drugs in a small piano

indicators.note: in means inside the following letters

parts.note: E for ecstasy, so a stash is several of them

explanation.surface: Someone dead with a large drugs stash hidden in a small piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead is the numb sense, as in a limb gone dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone numb is said to be dead or to have fallen into this state.

clue.text: Much-troubled Texan behind electronic parts firm

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the word is divided by other letters

parts.note: E for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A troubled Texan backs an electronic parts firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Electronic parts firm reads as a company; parts is the verb splitting firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harried and pestered is much troubled, so this adjective is a synonym.
